clue.text: Bit of dessert? Leading lady has something to chew over

indicators.note: the chewing material is placed over, so round, the leading lady

parts.note: cud is what a cow brings back up to chew again
a leading lady is the star of a show

explanation.surface: A diva at the dinner table is left mulling something over between bites.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a star brooding over a problem; 'over' is really the container signal, the cud going round the leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet sauce served as one component of a pudding, hence a bit of dessert.

clue.text: Stop shooting large animal with old side arm

parts.note: a film director shouts cut to stop the cameras shooting
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an ass is a donkey, an animal

explanation.surface: A hunter lays down the rifle beside a big beast and reaches for a period sidearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once carried by sailors, an antique weapon worn at the side.

clue.text: Bribe Frenchman to come back after dessert

indicators.note: the Frenchman's piece is placed after the dessert piece

parts.note: a sweet is the British word for a dessert course

indicators.note: coming back means the Frenchman's name is read from right to left

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A French visitor is asked to return once pudding is over, perhaps with a bribe in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' reverses the Frenchman's name; René is a stock French name in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is slang for a bribe, an inducement to make a deal more palatable.

clue.text: Change following demotion of head

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is demoted further down the word

parts.note: later means following, coming afterwards

explanation.surface: Things shift after the boss is demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The L at the head of LATER moves down one place to give ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change or modify it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Put out fizzy Diet Colas

indicators.note: fizzy suggests the letters bubbling about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a pair of sparkling diet colas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'annoyed', but it is the dislocating of a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a shoulder is to dislocate it, forcing the joint out of place.

clue.text: Manuscript about a pet dog

indicators.note: the manuscript abbreviation goes about, round, the a

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff

explanation.surface: A document describes a beloved animal companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' is not an animal but a sulk or quarrel, TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Vehicle used to be blue

definitions.meaning: past tense of mope: was gloomy or sulked

explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a small motor vehicle; moped is also the past tense of mope, to be glum.

clue.text: Strong support

definitions.meaning: binding with bands of material, as a strapped injury

explanation.definitionFit: Strapping means sturdily built, and as a noun is bands of material used to bind and support.

clue.text: Stroke? Grimace right away

indicators.note: the letter for right goes away from the word

parts.note: a rictus is a fixed grimace

explanation.surface: Someone stops pulling a face after a turn for the better.
explanation.definitionFit: An ictus is a medical seizure or stroke, and also the stressed beat in verse.

clue.text: Prevent from crossing over marsh

indicators.note: the crossing is laid over, so around, the marsh

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing
a fen is low marshy land

explanation.surface: Someone is stopped from wading across a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Forfend is an archaic verb meaning to avert or keep something from happening.

clue.text: Minister to provide free entertainment

definitions.meaning: attend to medically, as a doctor does a patient
pay for someone else's meal or drinks

explanation.definitionFit: To treat a patient is to minister to them; to treat friends is to pay for their outing.

clue.text: Celebrity redhead in pastures new

indicators.note: the head of red sits inside the reworked letters
new suggests the letters made new, rearranged

parts.note: the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A famous ginger moves to fresh fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PASTURES to SUPESTA..., with R slotted in to give SUPERSTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is an extremely famous performer, a top celebrity.

clue.text: Stern monarch has promise for rider

parts.note: aft means at the stern of a ship
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
to give your word is to promise

explanation.surface: A strict king gives a pledge to a horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' is not strict but the back of a ship; 'rider' is an addendum, not a horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to a document, so an afterword appended at the end.

clue.text: President backing oil company in pursuit of 14

indicators.note: backing means the oil company's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Esso is a well-known oil company brand

explanation.surface: A president supports a petrol firm as it chases a fugitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to chase an outlaw, the desperado of 14.

clue.text: Assembly given by extremely saintly head

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its outer letters

parts.note: to nod is to head the ball in football

explanation.surface: A gathering is addressed by a very pious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is the football verb, NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy and officials.

clue.text: Very old agents held up by outlaw

indicators.note: the agents are held inside the very old letters

parts.note: dead is informal British for very, as in dead easy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: reps are sales agents

explanation.surface: Ageing secret agents are delayed by a bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the agents in this down clue, and 'held' places them within; 'dead' for 'very' is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal, the classic Wild West outlaw.

clue.text: Chosen one paid tip — I left change

indicators.note: the I is left out of the pool of letters
change signals rearranging the remaining letters

explanation.surface: A selected person paid a gratuity, and someone gave change.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE PAID TIP, minus the I, rearranged gives APPOINTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Appointed means named or selected for a post, so chosen.

clue.text: Latin poet breaks promise

indicators.note: breaks suggests the words smashed and the letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A Roman writer fails to keep his word.
explanation.definitionFit: Potential is promise, the capacity to develop into something good.

clue.text: Target man flying Spitfire

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters scattered in the air

explanation.surface: A wartime pilot in a Spitfire is on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitfire' looks like the fighter plane; it is a fiery-tempered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing woman, a spitfire or shrew.

clue.text: Vehicle to pick up a passenger returning from chaotic situation

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembly is read backwards
the second word rides inside the vehicle as a passenger

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle on rails
to sense is to pick up, as with a signal

explanation.surface: A bus heads back from a riot, having collected someone along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a passenger' signals one piece riding inside the vehicle, and 'returning' reverses the whole; 'pick up' means detect, as a radio picks up a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a confused, disorderly muddle, or an illusory discovery.

clue.text: Made notes about very small dog lead

parts.note: minute means tiny

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone records details of a tiny puppy's leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a leash but picks the first letter of 'dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: To minute a meeting is to record notes of it in the official minutes.

clue.text: Pulls faces when soldiers hug sailors

indicators.note: the soldiers wrap round the sailors as in a hug

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Troops grimace as they embrace navy men.
explanation.definitionFit: To girn is a Scots and northern English word meaning to grimace or snarl.

clue.text: Boiled the egg outside

indicators.note: the egg word sits outside the word the

parts.note: a seed and an egg are both germs of new life

explanation.surface: Something was cooked with the egg in its shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boiled' suggests cooking; it means fumed with anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Seethed is an old past tense of seethe, to boil, and now means fumed.

clue.text: Bottle-opener very well hidden?

indicators.note: the letters are concealed across the words opener and very

explanation.surface: A corkscrew has been carefully tucked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle in British slang means courage, the guts to act.

clue.text: Leave head gardener missing plant product

indicators.note: the gardener's head is missing from the word

parts.note: to resign is to leave a job

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chief gardener quits, without a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance secreted by plants, especially conifers.

clue.text: Means of stopping playboy pursuing place to stay

indicators.note: pursuing means the playboy piece follows behind

parts.note: a B and B, bed and breakfast, is a place to stay
a rake is a dissolute playboy

explanation.surface: A womaniser chases a guest house, hoping to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: B and B is written as letters B, AND, B.
explanation.definitionFit: A band brake is a brake in which a band tightens round a drum, a mechanism to stop motion.

clue.text: Boy born on top of stretcher?

indicators.note: in a down clue the born letter sits on top of the boy

parts.note: B is the genealogical abbreviation for born
Rick is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A newborn lad lies on a medical stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: In bricklaying a stretcher is a brick laid lengthwise, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is one example of a brick, the one laid with its long side showing.

clue.text: Society embroiled by boom and bust

indicators.note: embroiled by means caught up inside the word boom

explanation.surface: A club is caught up in the economic cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boom and bust' suggests economics, but 'bust' is the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust and bosom both mean a woman's chest.

clue.text: Conductor has terrible constipation, broken pot taken away

indicators.note: terrible signals rearranging the letters
the letters of pot are taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: A maestro is stricken with blockage after his chamber vessel breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: CONSTIPATION less P, O and T rearranges to TOSCANINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Band recruits novice guitarist

indicators.note: the band takes in the novice as a recruit

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth
L is a learner, a novice, from L-plates

explanation.surface: A rock group takes on a beginner on guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group but is a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slash is the stage name of the Guns N' Roses guitarist.

clue.text: I can't help cook eviscerated bird

parts.note: dunno is informal for I don't know, a helpless reply

indicators.note: with its insides removed only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone declines to help gut a bird for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock is a small brown songbird, the hedge sparrow.

clue.text: Checked top worn by child

indicators.note: the top goes over the child, worn like a hat

parts.note: a lid is a top, as of a jar
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A tartan shirt is worn by a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked' suggests a pattern; it means restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked as in held back or restrained, so limited.
